Definition: strictly nothingness; also trouble. vanity, wickedness; specifically an idol
BiblicalUsage: Aven is nothingness that pretends to be something — vanity, trouble, wickedness, and by extension the idol itself. Samuel tells Saul rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft and stubbornness as iniquity and idolatry; Isaiah says God cannot endure the solemn meeting joined to iniquity; Proverbs pictures the naughty person walking with a froward mouth; Habakkuk cries out at the iniquity he sees on every side.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe aven is the right name for sin because sin is empty at its core — it promises weight and delivers nothing. That is why I hold fast to what is solid instead: God's word, which never turns out to be nothing.
